reason: The star is the central object, but the available pieces do not make the first stage unambiguous.
expectation: Its compatible partners should indicate how to begin building the stellar interior.

choice.with: Hydrogen nuclei in the stellar core

alternatives.reason: Hydrogen fusion is a plausible starting point, but I am not sure the star is its direct partner.

effect: Hydrogen fusion produced a helium-rich core, suggesting compression may drive the next stage.
reaction: The automatic combination made the first stage clear.
reason: Compression in the stellar core plausibly raises the temperature needed for helium fusion.
expectation: Compression should advance the core toward helium burning.

effect: Compression produced a helium-burning core, so helium is the likely next fuel to combine with it.
reaction: The distinction between nuclear burning and ordinary chemical heat is useful.
reason: Helium burning suggests combining the core with the available neutral helium.
expectation: Helium fusion should produce heavier material in the core.

effect: Helium burning produced carbon-rich material through the triple-alpha process; the core can now advance to a later burning stage.
reaction: The unstable intermediate makes the carbon-making process more interesting than a simple pairing.
reason: Further compression plausibly heats the carbon-rich material enough for the next stage of fusion.
expectation: Compression should advance the material toward carbon burning.

effect: Compression produced carbon-burning layers, with several heavier elements among their products.
reaction: The multiple reaction products make the stage more informative than a single-element progression.
reason: Further compression is a plausible way to reach the next hotter burning stage.
expectation: The layers should advance toward a later stage of stellar burning.

effect: Further compression produced oxygen-burning layers, which make silicon and sulfur while outer shells can keep burning.
reaction: The simultaneous burning shells clarify how the layered interior develops.
reason: Further compression plausibly advances the core to a hotter burning stage.
expectation: The layers should progress toward silicon burning and the end of fusion support.

effect: Compression produced silicon-burning material and was consumed; its reactions move nuclei toward the iron group.
reaction: The reaction network is more complex than a simple silicon fusion pairing.
reason: The obvious compression partner is gone, so checking the new material should reveal how to proceed.
expectation: Its available partners should indicate the next stage toward the iron-group core.

effect: Silicon-burning material has no available partner yet, so another part of the layered interior likely needs attention first.
reaction: I was surprised that the newest material could not be combined yet.
reason: The star may accept the accumulated burning layers to build its interior.
expectation: Its available partners should show whether the layers can be assembled around it.

alternatives.reason: The layers themselves may indicate how to assemble the interior.

effect: The star has no available partner, so the remaining layers must be combined another way.
reaction: The second empty compatibility list is mildly frustrating.
reason: Inspecting the carbon-burning layers may reveal how to assemble the interior.
expectation: Their available partners should indicate a way to build the layered interior.

effect: Combining the carbon- and oxygen-burning layers completed the layered interior; the remaining goal is the end of fusion support.
reaction: The coexisting shells make the onion metaphor clearer.
reason: Silicon-burning material drives reactions toward the iron group, so it plausibly advances the assembled interior toward an iron core.
expectation: The silicon-burning material should help bring the core toward the end of fusion support.

effect: The silicon-burning material brought the layered star to an iron-group core, completing the final goal and establishing why further fusion cannot sustain it.
reaction: The link between iron-group nuclei and the loss of fusion support was a satisfying conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the onion of burning shells clarified that different burning regions coexist within one star, rather than forming separate stars or pure shells.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the silicon-burning material and then the star yielded two empty compatibility lists, making the route to assembling the layers briefly frustrating.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the newest silicon-burning material had no available partner until the other burning layers were assembled.

arbitrary.text: The need to combine the carbon- and oxygen-burning layers first was not obvious when the silicon-burning material appeared, although the resulting shell metaphor gave the action a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the approaching core collapse unfolds, especially because the chapter connected the stellar layers to their physical processes.
